Article Title: IIT-Bombay student suicide case: Institute apologises over earlier remarks; student affairs dean suspended
Article Text:
IIT Bombay suspends Dean Suryanarayana Doolla

MUMBAI: IIT-Bombay placed Prof Suryanarayana Doolla on immediate suspension from his deanship, following continued students' protests on campus for the last three days. Prof Doolla was the dean of administrative affairs. He was accused of abetment of Sahil Wakode's death by suicide. Wakode's family also filed a case of harassment against him under the Atrocities Act. The institute issued a public apology on their social media handle, after students accused them of 'defaming' Wakode, without carrying out a detailed inquiry."We apologise for the statements contained in our earlier communication concerning the circumstances surrounding the unfortunate demise of Sahil," it said. "The details and circumstances leading up to the incident remain subject to investigation by the appropriate authorities. In view of the ongoing investigation, it was inappropriate to have set out or characterised details relating to the events preceding his demise before they had been duly established through the appropriate investigative process," the institute added. The administration also denied the allegations of the director's resignation, after videos of him from the protest went viral.In a mail sent to the campus residents, the institute director, Prof Shireesh Kedare, mentioned, 'the deanship of Prof Suryanarayan Doolla is suspended with immediate effect. Any further action will be taken after investigation'. Doolla has not been suspended from his professorship at the energy science and engineering department.A meeting of the institute's Board of Governors is underway.The students submitted a charter of 18 demands on Sunday night in a meeting with the director and the institute functionaries, which went on for three hours. The director signed the charter. Students pressed on the suspension of Prof Doolla and an apology along with 16 other demands.In the list of demands raised by the students' groups on the campus, the students have demanded an an independent investigation committee, with student representatives and external members recommended by students, suspension of officials who are found guilty after the investigation, a fair compensation for the families.Among the many demands, the students have also sought a code of conduct and sensitisation for professors.The director signed the list of demands on the live recording, though officials refused to comment. An open house with students is expected to be scheduled today.Protests erupted on the Powai campus on Friday night after Wakode, a second-year student of energy science and engineering, ended his life hours after he was caught using a mobile phone during the institute’s mid-semester examination. He allegedly uploaded the exam paper on an AI platform for answers. This is the third case of suicide on the campus this year.While the institute, in a statement, mentioned that no action was initiated against Wakode, many claimed that he was threatened with suspension.
Article Summary: IIT Bombay suspends Dean Suryanarayana Doolla. He was accused of abetment of Sahil Wakode's death by suicide. The students submitted a charter of 18 demands on Sunday night in a meeting with the director and the institute functionaries, which went on for three hours.

Article Title: 'Delhi a terrifying daily story for women': Rahul, Priyanka slam Amit Shah over teen's gangrape-murder
Article Text:
Rahul directly questioned Shah over the responsibility for women's safety in Delhi. Priyanka Gandhi further questioned the government's response to crimes against women.

What happened in Delhi case

NEW DELHI: Congress leaders Rahul Gandhi and Priyanka Gandhi Vadra have spoken out over the alleged gang rape and murder of a teenage girl in Delhi, with both questioning the authorities over women's safety and demanding accountability for the incident.Rahul Gandhi, leader of opposition in Lok Sabha, criticised the Delhi Police and questioned the responsibility of Union home minister Amit Shah, under whose ministry the force functions. He said the teenager was gang-raped and murdered before her body was dumped in an open field, and questioned how the police remained unaware of the crime for days.In a post on X, Rahul Gandhi described the incident as a "horrific act of brutality" in the national capital. He also dismissed the idea that Delhi was providing women with a safe environment, saying the city had instead become a source of fear for women."It's unfortunate that Delhi is no longer the capital today; it has become a terrifying daily story for women," he said.Rahul directly questioned Shah over the responsibility for women's safety in Delhi. He pointed out that the Delhi Police is under the Union home ministry and asked who should ultimately be held responsible for the safety of women in the capital."Amit Shah ji, Delhi Police is under your control. Ultimately, whose responsibility is women's safety?" he said.He also criticised the functioning of the Delhi Police, asking whether its role had been reduced to intimidating ordinary citizens while criminals continued to operate without fear."Or has the job of Delhi Police been reduced to just intimidating and threatening ordinary citizens? Because the criminals are roaming around fearlessly," Gandhi said.Calling for immediate action, the Congress leader demanded that those responsible for the crime be arrested and punished strictly. He also sought accountability for what he described as criminal negligence."The beasts must be arrested immediately, strict action and punishment must be taken, and accountability for this criminal negligence must be fixed," he said.Rahul Gandhi ended his post by linking women's safety to India's wider progress, saying, "India cannot move forward without women's safety."Priyanka Gandhi also raised concerns over the case, saying the crime against the teenager represented an extreme form of brutality. She noted that another minor girl had allegedly been raped just days earlier and questioned whether authorities were taking sufficient responsibility for women's safety."In Delhi, all limits of cruelty were crossed against a 17-year-old girl, and after that, she was brutally murdered. Just a few days earlier, another minor girl was raped," she said in a post on X.Priyanka Gandhi further questioned the government's response to crimes against women. She argued that while there was discussion about women's development, women continued to face violence without what she described as concrete action against perpetrators."No one in the country is willing to take responsibility for women's safety—only empty talk about women's development is offered," she said.She claimed that hundreds of women face atrocities and violence and alleged that victims can struggle to get action from authorities, including the registration of FIRs."Hundreds of women face atrocities and violence, but they cannot hope for concrete action against the perpetrators—FIRs aren't even filed," she said.Priyanka Gandhi also said the issue went beyond the individual case and reflected a wider failure to ensure women's basic rights. She argued that both society and the government had failed to provide women with adequate safety, freedom and equality."Both society and the government have completely failed in granting women their rights to safety, freedom, and equality," she said.A teenage girl was allegedly gang-raped and murdered in Delhi. Her body was subsequently dumped in an open field, with the police facing questions over the delay in detecting the crime.The case has triggered political criticism over women's safety in the capital, with Rahul Gandhi focusing on the Delhi Police's role and its accountability to the Union home ministry.Priyanka Gandhi also referred to another case involving a minor girl that was reported days before the teenager's rape and murder. She used the two incidents to question the wider response to crimes against women.
Article Summary: A teenage girl was allegedly gang-raped and murdered in Delhi. Her body was subsequently dumped in an open field. The case has triggered political criticism over women's safety in the capital. Congress leaders Rahul Gandhi and Priyanka Gandhi Vadra have spoken out over the alleged gang rape and murder of a teenage girl.

NEW DELHI: Congress spokesperson Shama Mohamed on Monday expressed solidarity with an IIT Bombay professor accused by the father of a second-year BTech student of harassing his son, saying that students in her generation were “mentally strong”.The student, from IIT Bombay’s Department of Energy Science and Engineering, allegedly died by suicide on Friday evening after he was found using a mobile phone during a mid-semester examination.The Mumbai Police has transferred the case to the Crime Branch after the student’s father filed a complaint alleging that IIT Bombay professor and exam invigilator Suryanarayana Doolla had hurled casteist slurs at his son over the past three months. An FIR has been registered against Doolla.Reacting to the controversy, Mohamed wrote: “In this suicide, I stand with Professor Doolla. If a student is caught cheating, it is normal to admonish him & ask him to leave the room. If the student was harassed due to his caste, he should have complained to the SC/ST department.”She added: “When we were kids - we were admonished by teachers, parents for our wrongdoings but our generation was mentally strong.”Mohamed also called for greater mental health support for students, writing: “I would request colleges to have mental health therapists for the wellbeing of the students.”According to IIT Bombay, the student was found with a mobile phone in the examination hall and had uploaded the question paper on ChatGPT to seek answers. The institute said no disciplinary action had been initiated against him.The IIT Bombay Faculty Forum has also expressed solidarity with Doolla, saying he was following institute-approved procedures after detecting the alleged academic malpractice. It said the professor reported the incident to the authorities for further action.The institute said Doolla and the Head of Department had counselled the student and assured him that the incident would not adversely affect his academic career. The student subsequently returned to his hostel room, where he was later found dead.The incident has since triggered student protests on campus, with students demanding accountability and transparency from the administration.
Article Summary: Congress spokesperson Shama Mohamed expresses solidarity with IIT Bombay professor. Suryanarayana Doolla is accused by the father of a second-year BTech student of harassing his son. The student allegedly died by suicide on Friday evening after he was found using a mobile phone during a mid-semester examination.

NEW DELHI: IIT Bombay is planning to replace ceiling fans with wall-mounted fans in its student hostels, with sources saying the move had been under consideration for the past two months and was recently finalised. Students also claimed that the first batch of wall-mounted fans had arrived on campus.The replacement was among the measures the institute had assured students it would undertake in July. It followed the death by suicide of another student.This comes amid an ongoing row over the death of 20-year-old BTech second-year student Sahil Wakode on the institute campus.Sahil was found dead in his hostel room on Friday after he was allegedly caught using a mobile phone during an examination. IIT Bombay, however, said no disciplinary action had been initiated against him and that he was counselled and assured that the incident would not affect his academic career.IIT Bombay has maintained that no disciplinary action was initiated against Sahil and that he was counselled and assured that the incident would not affect his academic career.IIT Bombay director Shireesh Kedare also denied allegations of caste-based discrimination at the institute, saying students’ caste-related information is kept confidential and is not accessible to faculty or administrators. The institute’s SC/ST cell said it had not received any complaint from Sahil alleging caste discrimination.Meanwhile, IIT Bombay director Kedare also held a late-night, three-hour meeting on Sunday with students who had gathered in large numbers at the institute’s main gate to protest the death by suicide of BTech student Sahil Wakode, 20.During the meeting, which students recorded live, the institute administration discussed and signed a list of 18 demands put forward by the protesters. An institute official said the discussions would continue and that “due process will be followed”.The institute’s Board of Governors is scheduled to meet on Monday to discuss the issue, while an open house with students is also expected to be held the same day.

Article Title: Yemeni national attacks Sikh bus driver in Telford, smashes & hijacks vehicle
Article Text:
Sikh bus driver attacked and thrown from vehicle in England; hijacked bus crashes into multiple cars before suspect is arrested.

LONDON: A 33-year-old Yemeni national was arrested for allegedly assaulting a British Sikh bus driver, vandalising the vehicle, hijacking it and crashing the bus into multiple vehicles in Telford, in England’s West Midlands region, last week.The unprovoked attack occurred around 6.37pm at Court Street in Madeley, Shropshire, on Sept 18. Video footage shared by a bystander showed the accused, Ali Balhad, grabbing the driver, punching him and tugging at his beard. The attacker was seen pulling out the cash register and hurling it at the driver.Throughout the ordeal, the driver appeared calm, holding on to his beard and begging people around to call the police. “Just take this guy away from me,” he was heard saying.To distract the attacker, Kymberlee Daley (19), who filmed the assault, told him that she had called the police, allowing the driver to jump out of the bus window and flee. To her horror, Balhad took the wheel and started driving the single-decker bus the wrong way down the street.The bus collided with multiple vehicles before coming to a stop, even as shocked bystanders chased it.Armed officers arrived at the scene within 10 minutes and arrested Balhad, who had been in Telford for about a week. He was charged with aggravated vehicle taking; assault; attempted grievous bodily harm; driving a motor vehicle dangerously; robbery; theft from a store; threats to kill; and three counts of criminal damage. The accused was remanded in custody and is due to appear before Telford Magistrates’ Court Monday.Paramedics treated the bus driver for minor injuries, West Mercia police said.
Article Summary: A 33-year-old Yemeni national was arrested for allegedly assaulting a British Sikh bus driver. Video footage showed the accused, Ali Balhad, grabbing the driver, punching him and tugging at his beard. Balhad then took the wheel and started driving the single-decker bus the wrong way down the street.

Article Title: BJP, Congress trade barbs over PM Modi mimicry at Rahul Gandhi’s Indore event
Article Text:
PM Modi mimicry at Rahul Gandhi event

BJP leaders hit out at Rahul Gandhi

Congress leaders defend programme

NEW DELHI: BJP on Sunday criticised the Congress after stand-up comedian Pulkit Mani mimicked Prime Minister Narendra Modi during an event attended by party leader Rahul Gandhi in Madhya Pradesh, with Union ministers and other BJP leaders targeting the opposition party and Congress MP over the performance.The comedian performed the skit with the Rae Bareli MP during the latest edition of the ‘Chhatron Ki Goonj’ event in Indore on Saturday. A video of the performance was shared by the Congress on X.In the short act, Mani came on stage laughing and hugged Rahul. “My friend. How are you?” he said. The Congress leader replied, “I'm fine; how are you, Modi ji?” Mani responded, “Great harassment”, and continued laughing while repeatedly using the phrase “my friend”.Rahul then said, “Very nice to meet you,” and asked Mani to “tell me more”. The comedian continued laughing and hugging Gandhi before saying, “Maa ko kursi do, maa”, while pointing towards the audience.Union minister Piyush Goyal reacted to the performance on X, calling Rahul “Asanskari naraz fufa (uncultured disgruntled uncle).”“The irony writes itself. The need to come on stage every now and then just to drag Prime Minister Modi ji's name into cheap political theatre never fails to amaze me,” Goyal said, asking the former Congress president to “look in the mirror”.Union minister Kiren Rijiju also criticised Rahul, saying, “I hadn't imagined that a party which was in power for nearly six decades would turn into such a circus that is busy entertaining their own shrunken supporters.”Rijiju said Indians were proud that Prime Minister Modi was the “most popular” elected leader in the world.“Congress party has become a party of comedians and Jokers! They are out forever.... RIP,” he said.“Do you feel absolutely no shame in mocking an elderly mother and the Prime Minister of India?” Rijiju asked Rahul, while posting a video of PM Modi in which the prime minister is seen asking for a chair for an elderly woman who had attended one of his programmes.BJP national general secretary Smriti Irani also reacted to the controversy, writing in Hindi on X, “Jab nash manuj per chata hai, pehle vivek mar jaata hai” (When doom looms over a person, it's his conscience that dies first).BJP national secretary Sandeep Pathak called the mimicry act an expression of “desperation” and the “growing intellectual bankruptcy” of the Congress.“When you lose touch with India's values, you lose touch with India itself. And that is precisely where the Congress has lost its way,” Pathak, a Rajya Sabha MP, said on X.Congress leader Bhupesh Baghel hit back at the BJP's criticism, saying every person's mother deserved respect and questioning why similar concerns were not raised when the mothers of Rahul and other leaders were allegedly insulted.“Everyone's mother is a mother, not PM Modi's mother alone. Why are their feelings not hurt when they insult Rahul Gandhi's mother or other leaders' mothers? This culture of insulting mothers was started by BJP-RSS and Mahamanav,” Baghel said.Congress MP Imraan Masood said the ‘Chhatron Ki Goonj’ programme had “shattered eardrums” of BJP leaders.“Let the elections come. They will find out soon enough. 'Chhatron Ki Goonj' has shattered their eardrums. They see Rahul Gandhi in their dreams and wake up with a start,” Masood said in Ranchi.Congress leader TS Singh Deo said criticism and mimicry should not be objected to, but opposed the use of abusive language in public conversations.“I do not think it is acceptable to stoop to the level of abusive language in a public conversation. But beyond that, if you're criticising someone in a normal way, even in a joking manner or with mimicry, no one should have any objection to it,” he said in Raipur.AICC general secretary Ghulam Ahmad Mir said the programme had received an overwhelming response and claimed that more than 200,000 young people had attended events under the initiative across India and Madhya Pradesh.Rahul Gandhi had addressed students at the Indore session on issues including education costs and employment opportunities.Congress leaders said the programme was focused on issues faced by young people and student welfare.
Article Summary: Comedian Pulkit Mani mimicked Prime Minister Narendra Modi during an event attended by party leader Rahul Gandhi in Madhya Pradesh. The comedian performed the skit with the Rae Bareli MP during the latest edition of the ‘Chhatron Ki Goonj’ event.

Article Title: ‘Why are students forced to live in unsafe PGs?’ Rahul Gandhi after Satya Niketan tragedy
Article Text:

What's the Satya Niketan tragedy?

NEW DELHI: Lok Sabha LoP and Congress leader Rahul Gandhi on Sunday questioned the system over the Satya Niketan tragedy, asking who would take responsibility for the death of Arpit Jhaj and other students.In an X post, Gandhi said Arpit’s grieving family is seeking answers after his death, asking, “What was that innocent one’s fault?”Gandhi said Arpit’s family was forced to leave their son in an unsafe place because of the lack of adequate and safe hostels for students. He questioned whether the tragedy could have been avoided had safety standards been properly followed.“The system’s irresponsibility and corruption have snatched away many lives full of dreams and devastated many families filled with hope,” Gandhi said.He said Arpit’s family, as well as the country, is demanding accountability and responsibility for students’ safety to be fixed so that no parent has to endure such a loss again.Gandhi also questioned why new and safe hostels were not being built and why students were being forced to live in unsafe PG accommodations.He further sought an update on the investigation into the Satya Niketan incident, asking: “How far has the investigation into the Satya Niketan incident progressed?”The building at Satya Niketan, which housed a boys’ PG accommodation near Delhi University ’s South Campus, collapsed on September 6.The incident claimed lives of seven students. The tragedy renewed questions over the safety of private PGs and hostels, particularly those operating from old residential buildings.The Delhi High Court has also expressed concern over the safety of students living in PGs and private hostels and questioned the regulatory framework governing such establishments and ordered a high-level MCD inquiry.It said the collapse of a multi-storey hostel building in Satya Niketan, which killed seven people including students, was "not an ordinary incident."“Four students lost their lives in the mishap...very tragic. It's not an ordinary incident of any mishap. These four students had come to the capital with a lot of hopes and dreams, coming from small towns. All of that was shattered by such callous and criminal conduct on the part of (certain persons),” the court said.
Article Summary: Lok Sabha LoP and Congress leader Rahul Gandhi questioned the system over the Satya Niketan tragedy. He asked who would take responsibility for the death of Arpit Jhaj and other students. Gandhi said Arpit’s family was forced to leave their son in an unsafe place.

NEW DELHI: With Uttar Pradesh set for assembly polls in 2027, AIMIM supremo Asaduddin Owaisi has thrown open the possibility of an alliance with parties looking to prevent the BJP from returning to power for a third straight term, saying no opposition party can take on the BJP alone.Owaisi, speaking to news agency ANI on Sunday, invited “like-minded” parties for talks and said AIMIM was prepared to work with them if the common objective was to keep the BJP out of power.“We do not want the BJP government to be formed for a third time in Uttar Pradesh. If anyone does not want the BJP to form the government, they can talk to us. We are ready to work with you to stop the BJP from coming to power. But it is important to understand that you cannot stop the BJP alone,” he said.His outreach comes as political parties begin preparing for the 2027 contest in Uttar Pradesh, where the BJP has been in power since 2017 under the leadership of Yogi Adityanath Owaisi, however, cautioned against viewing the coming election through the lens of previous polls, saying the political contest would have its own set of challenges.“Assembly elections are coming. It won’t be the 2014 election, nor the 2017 election, nor the 2019 election, nor the 2022 election.This is going to be a completely different election,” he said.Owaisi pointed to AIMIM’s experience in Bihar to underline the party’s position on alliances. He said the party had approached several opposition leaders before the Bihar elections , seeking an alliance and asking for six seats, but the proposal did not find support.“We said this in Bihar as well, and our president, Akhtarul Iman, wrote a letter not just to the RJD or the Congress, but to all the CPI and Communist Party leaders. We said, ‘Please give us six seats.’ But they did not agree,” he said.Despite the lack of an alliance, Owaisi said AIMIM would continue building its organisation in Uttar Pradesh. He claimed the party’s leadership had developed from the grassroots and said its workers were already active across constituencies.“Our party organisation has become quite strong. Our leadership has emerged at the grassroots level, and our leaders have a strong connection with the ground. The party is working hard on its part,” he said.Hyderabad MP said alliance talks would not determine AIMIM’s organisational plans.“Whether we are in talks with whom or not is a different matter, but we will continue our work. If you want to stop the BJP, come and talk to us. We are ready to work with you,” he said.Turning to the Yogi-led BJP government, Owaisi alleged that several promises made by the party remained unfulfilled. He raised issues including governance, law and order, electricity and land disputes, saying these would become important themes in the election.He also criticised the previous Samajwadi Party government, drawing a comparison between the two regimes.“When the Samajwadi Party was in power, one kind of hooliganism used to happen. Someone else did it. Now, under their government, a different kind of hooliganism is happening,” Owaisi said.He also sought the public release of the SIT report into the alleged Ram Mandir embezzlement case and questioned how accused persons were securing bail.“Why isn’t the SIT report released to the public? Why doesn’t the government release it? And why are those people getting bail? How are they getting bail? It’s strange. This will also be a big talking point,” he said.AIMIM has already begun preparing for the 2027 election, with Owaisi saying the party is touring constituencies to strengthen its organisation and gauge local concerns.He said he was in Kanpur on Sunday and would visit Shravasti in six days, followed by Azamgarh. Public meetings are also planned in three or four constituencies in western Uttar Pradesh.“The sole purpose is to strengthen our party organisation for the upcoming elections,” Owaisi said.He added that staying connected with voters was central to the party’s preparations.“By staying among the people, we can understand their suffering on the ground and highlight the difficulties this government has created for them,” he said.
Article Summary: AIMIM supremo Asaduddin Owaisi has thrown open the possibility of an alliance with parties looking to prevent the BJP from returning to power for a third straight term. He invited ‘like-minded’ parties for talks and said AIMIM was prepared to work with them if the common objective was to keep the BJP out of power.

NEW DELHI: Former Tamil Nadu BJP president K Annamalai on Sunday said he “completely rejects” the "atheistic and anti-Brahmin" ideologies espoused by EV Ramasamy, popularly known as “Periyar,” while acknowledging the Dravidian stalwart's contributions to women’s empowerment and the fight against caste discrimination.“We acknowledge that he (Periyar) advocated women’s liberation and spoke about the eradication of caste. NEW DELHI: The death toll from the attack on the police lines headquarters in Kohat, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, rose to at least 31, with over 100 injured, as military and police forces concluded the 22-hour-long stand-off Saturday noon.What began on Friday as a suicide blast at the compound's perimeter gate rapidly developed into an active siege after at least seven operatives from the Ittehad-ul-Mujahideen Pakistan (IMP) group breached the counter terrorism department (CTD) and intelligence facilities. Khyber Police claimed to have neutralised eight of the attackers. Article Title: 'Prisoner No. 626710 is Present': CBFC flags Umar Khalid film screening at IIIT-Hyderabad
Article Text:
Umar Khalid





HYDERABAD: The Central Board of Film Certification (CBFC) objected to the proposed screening of a documentary on jailed activist Umar Khalid at IIIT-Hyderabad, saying screening an uncertified film would violate the Cinematograph Act unless an exemption had been granted, according to news agency PTI reported.The documentary, "Prisoner No. 626710 is Present", directed by filmmaker Lalit Vachani, was proposed to be screened by a group of students at the institute's KRB Auditorium at 8 pm on Friday. Sources said the students have now decided to cancel the screening."Public screening of a documentary film that has not yet been certified by the CBFC is a violation of the Cinematograph Act unless a specific exemption has been sought under the Act," the CBFC posted on X.Tagging IIIT-Hyderabad, the CBFC said the institute's authorities "may take note for necessary action".The CBFC functions under the Union Information and Broadcasting Ministry.IIIT-H, however, distanced itself from the proposed screening, saying neither the institute nor any of its recognised student bodies had organised or hosted a screening of an uncertified film.In a statement, the institute said it "categorically clarifies that neither the Institute nor any of its recognised student clubs, cells or organisations has organised or hosted any screening of any film uncertified by the Central Board of Film Certification"."IIIT Hyderabad has established processes governing official events and activities on campus, and any claim attributing an unauthorised or unrelated activity to the Institute or its recognised student bodies is factually incorrect," it said.The institute said students and faculty from its large and diverse community may meet or interact with people in their individual capacities."Such personal interactions or visits, where they occur, should not be construed as Institute-organised events, nor do they represent the views or activities of the Institute," it said.The development comes days after a proposed screening of the same documentary at the National Law School of India University (NLSIU) in Bengaluru was postponed following opposition from the RSS-affiliated Akhil Bharatiya Vidyarthi Parishad (ABVP).The NLSIU screening, organised by its student-run Law and Society Committee, was scheduled for September 14 to mark Political Prisoners' Day and six years of Khalid's incarceration.The ABVP had demanded that the screening be cancelled, alleging that allowing it would amount to using the campus for political propaganda.The student committee later postponed the programme citing "logistical and security considerations". It maintained that it was not backing out because of pressure and said the screening would be held later in the trimester."Prisoner No. 626710 is Present" centres on Khalid, a former Jawaharlal Nehru University research scholar who was arrested in September 2020 in connection with the alleged larger conspiracy behind the northeast Delhi riots.Khalid has been charged under the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act and other provisions in the case and has remained in custody since his arrest.The invitation for the proposed IIIT-H screening said it was planned on the occasion of "Political Prisoners' Day".It also referred to the anniversary of the death of revolutionary Jatindra Nath Das, a comrade of Bhagat Singh who died after a prolonged hunger strike in Lahore jail in 1929.
Article Summary: The Central Board of Film Certification (CBFC) objected to the proposed screening of a documentary on jailed activist Umar Khalid at IIIT-Hyderabad. The documentary, "Prisoner No. 626710 is Present", directed by filmmaker Lalit Vachani, was proposed to be screened by a group of students at the institute's KRB Auditorium at 8 pm on Friday. Sources said the students have now decided to cancel the screening.
