At least three people were killed and several others injured in a Pakistani airstrike targeting Afghanistan's northeastern Kunar province, Tolo News reported on Monday, citing a provincial official.The military strike is supposedly in retaliation for suicide bombing at a police station compound in northwestern Pakistan, raising fears that tensions between the neighbouring nations could once again turn into open fighting.Pakistan and Afghanistan were involved in their most serious military confrontation in years in February. The latest escalation comes days after the Taliban warned that it would defend Afghan territory against any Pakistani military action.Taliban spokesperson Zabihullah Mujahid, ahead of the imminent Pakistani strikes, had warned Islamabad against carrying out strikes inside Afghanistan, saying Kabul would respond militarily if its territory is attacked.In an interview with Al Arabiya English, Mujahid rejected Pakistan's allegations that militant groups based in Afghanistan recruit, train and launch attacks against Pakistan.“If Pakistan invokes Article 51 to violate the sanctity of Afghan territory, Afghanistan has the right to defend its country, and we will do so,” Mujahid said.He said any Pakistani military operation inside Afghanistan would amount to a violation of Afghan sovereignty and could trigger a strong response from Kabul.Mujahid was responding to comments by a Pakistani military spokesperson, who had told Al Arabiya English that militant groups were using Afghan territory to recruit, train and arm fighters before sending them into Pakistan.Mujahid rejected those allegations and said the Taliban administration does not allow the Tehreek-e-Taliban Pakistan , or TTP, to operate from Afghan soil.He also denied that the Taliban government supports armed groups carrying out attacks against other countries. Instead, Mujahid said Pakistan should examine its own internal security problems, arguing that violence involving the TTP and Baloch armed groups existed before the Taliban returned to power in 2021.Pakistan has repeatedly accused militant groups of operating from Afghanistan and has pressed Kabul to take action against them. The Taliban has consistently denied allowing Afghan territory to be used for attacks against Pakistan.Despite his warning of military retaliation, Mujahid said Kabul was still willing to engage with Islamabad through dialogue.He called for stronger intelligence-sharing arrangements and greater bilateral cooperation to address security concerns along the two countries' border.Mujahid also backed a possible mediation role for Saudi Arabia, saying Riyadh has good relations with both Afghanistan and Pakistan and could help the two sides resolve their differences.Relations between Kabul and Islamabad have remained strained over militant activity along their shared border. The latest airstrike, coming amid fresh security concerns, risks further worsening those ties and could lead to another confrontation between the neighbours.
Article Summary: Pakistan and Afghanistan were involved in their most serious military confrontation in years in February. The latest escalation comes days after the Taliban warned that it would defend Afghan territory against any Pakistani military action. Relations between Kabul and Islamabad have remained strained over militant activity along their shared border.

Article Title: 'Money works in elections': CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke on DUSU polls, campaigners in luxury cars
Article Text:
Abhijeet Dipke expresses concerns over the corrupting influence of money in DUSU elections





CHHATRAPATI SAMBHAJINAGAR: Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) founder Abhijeet Dipke on Sunday alleged that money power plays a major role in elections, citing the recent Delhi University Students' Union polls and claiming that campaigners arrive in luxury cars.He also accused the government of allowing ideological influence in educational institutions, questioned the examination system and announced fresh campaigns on issues involving MPSC aspirants and tribal schools.The ABVP , an affiliate of the Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS), won three of the four central panel posts in the Delhi University Students' Union polls held after recent CJP-led Gen Z protests.The Congress-backed National Students' Union of India ( NSUI ) failed to win any of the four central panel posts, with the ABVP securing the president, secretary and joint secretary positions.Asked about the DUSU polls, Dipke told reporters on Sunday evening, ''Money works in elections and nothing else. Those who campaign in DU come in Rolls Royce, which is worth crores of rupees. They come in Audi, BMW. So money works there.''On Congress MP Rahul Gandhi's claim that the BJP-led government was promoting people with ideological affiliations, Dipke raised similar concerns.''In Amravati, I saw that Vice Chancellor Kumud Sharma (VC of Mahatma Gandhi Antarrashtriya Hindi Vishwavidyalaya, Wardha, located near Amravati) comes from the RSS ideology.Since she became VC, FIRs have been registered against more than 50 students," he claimed."When students protest for something, an FIR is registered against them. But when ABVP opposes something or locks any gate, no FIR is registered against them. Only Dalit, Adivasi (tribal) students who oppose the ideology are booked.It is a roadmap to make institutions (universities) a shakha of RSS,'' Dipke charged.The CJP founder also claimed that students were losing faith in the education system.''The Maharashtra Public Service Commission aspirants have been demanding the resignation of MPSC Chairman Vivek Bhimanwar for many days (over allegations of corruption) and are agitating for it. The students have lost faith in the examination system. How can the students keep faith that exams will be conducted transparently until Bhimanwar resigns?'' he asked.Dipke said the CJP, along with MPSC aspirants, will soon launch an online campaign - 'Bhimanwar Rajinama Dya' (Bimanwar resign) - in which students will explain who Bhimanwar is, what his "achievements" are, his relation with Maharashtra Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis and why his resignation is required.On the suicide of an IIT Bombay student last week, Dipke said the incident could not be justified simply because the student was caught cheating.The student was found hanging from the ceiling fan in his hostel room on Friday evening, hours after he was allegedly caught using a mobile phone and ChatGPT during a mid-semester examination, as per officials.''The suicide incident at IIT Bombay is painful. This is a result of students losing faith in the education system. Children are dying in backward areas as well as big cities. They are committing suicide because they feel that no one is there to support them," Dipke claimed."Suicide cannot be justified if he is caught cheating. Did we ever hear of a minister committing suicide after being caught in corruption, or a businessman who looted a bank and fled? Mental health counselling is more important here. It was not such a grave mistake to warrant suicide," he said.Talking about his recent tour to Vidarbha, where he also visited tribal schools, the CJP leader alleged that students were not being provided proper facilities.''Ashram schools (residential schools) get a large amount of funds. Recently three students died of snakebite (in Gadchiroli), but still beds are not given to students, and they are still sleeping on the ground. Girls had to bathe in the open, and there was no roof or doors to the boys' bathroom. Are they animals?'' he asked.''If you cannot give a dignified education, then for what reason are you sitting in power? Dipke said, targeting the government.He further said the 'Adivasi School Thik Karo' campaign will continue and expand nationwide."I have visited parts of Maharashtra and will also go to Gujarat, about which no one is asking me,'' he added.(With PTI inputs)
Article Summary: Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) founder Abhijeet Dipke alleged that money power plays a major role in elections. He also accused the government of allowing ideological influence in educational institutions. Dipke announced fresh campaigns on issues involving MPSC aspirants and tribal schools.

Article Title: 'Broke into house, forced them into vehicles': Imran Khan’s son alleges aunts, cousins 'abducted' in Pakistan
Article Text:
Pakistani Police has already arrested ex-PM Imran Khan's sister in Lahore ahead of party's planned march. (Reuters photo)

More relatives allegedly detained

Aleema's detention ahead of PTI march

Poll Vote & Share your view Do you believe that the recent detentions of PTI members are politically motivated? Yes, definitely No, they're justified 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

Days before Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf's planned September 27 protest march, former prime minister Imran Khan 's son Kasim Khan has alleged that several members of his extended family have been detained and that their whereabouts have not been disclosed.In a series of posts on X, Kasim alleged that his aunts Dr Uzma and Noreen, along with cousins Shershah and Shahrez, were taken from their homes after authorities allegedly entered the properties and forced them into vehicles. The claims could not be independently verified.“This is a disgrace. Now my Aunts Dr. Uzma and Noureen, along with my cousins Shershah and Shahrez have now been abducted as well,” Kasim said.“They have broken into my aunties and cousins houses and forced them into vehicles with no explanation. No reasons for arrest have been stated. No news has been released as to where they have been taken,” he alleged.Kasim described the alleged detentions as “criminal behaviour” and called for international attention to the matter.Kasim later said the two children of Shahrez, aged four and six, had initially been missing. He subsequently said the children were safe but alleged that two more cousins, Azeem and Sakeenah, had also been taken into custody.“Hearing news that my cousin’s children are now safe. Meanwhile, two more of my cousins have been arrested. Azeem and Sakeenah. No reasons given. No location given,” he said.The allegations follow the detention of Imran Khan's sister Aleema Khan in Lahore on Sunday. She was ordered to be held for 30 days under the Punjab Maintenance of Public Order Ordinance, with the authorities citing public safety and order concerns. She was later taken to Kot Lakhpat jail, according to police and Pakistani media reports.Lahore deputy commissioner Muhammad Ali Ijaz issued the detention order under the MPO law. The order cited allegations involving protests, roadblocks and the mobilisation of PTI workers.PTI chairman barrister Gohar Ali Khan condemned Aleema's detention and demanded her release, arguing that it could further increase tensions ahead of the September 27 demonstration.Aleema's son Shahrez had earlier alleged that his mother was “abducted” after leaving her home and said the family had no information about where she had been taken.The PTI march is being organised to demand the release of Imran Khan, who remains in jail and is facing multiple legal cases. Pakistani authorities have stepped up measures against PTI supporters ahead of the planned protest.Meanwhile, Pakistani media have reported that Imran Khan underwent a medical check-up in jail amid continuing concerns raised by his family over his health.The government has cited public-order concerns in relation to Aleema Khan's detention, while PTI and members of Imran Khan's family have disputed the action and demanded information about those taken into custody.
Article Summary: Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf's planned September 27 protest march. Imran Khan's son Kasim Khan has alleged that several members of his extended family have been detained and that their whereabouts have not been disclosed. The allegations follow the detention of Imran Khan's sister Aleema Khan on Sunday.

Article Title: Realtor found dead in Audi in Bengaluru, cops suspect cardiac arrest
Article Text:
The Audi SUV in which Saleem was found dead being inspected by Koramangala police





BENGALURU: An Audi SUV parked outside a fast-food restaurant close to Koramangala police station triggered the alarm Sunday morning after the eatery staff found a man unresponsive inside the vehicle.Police have identified the deceased as Saleem Akbar S (46), a real estate businessman from Kodagu, who was staying in a Koramangala hotel.He was driving the Audi, which had reportedly arrived near Sagar Fast Food at 2.36am while it was raining.The restaurant staff who arrived in the early hours noticed the SUV and found a man inside.The SUV door was open, and when staff tried to wake the occupant, there was no response. They informed Koramangala police, who rushed to the spot and inspected the vehicle.According to investigators, Saleem may have died of a cardiac arrest, though the exact cause of death will be established through a postmortem examination.His body has been shifted to St John’s Hospital, a senior officer said. Saleem had rented a house at Koramangala. He had later shifted to another place before staying in the hotel.Police have contacted his family, who reside in Kodagu, and are also gathering more details about him and the circumstances preceding his death.A case of unnatural death has been registered. A postmortem examination will be conducted Monday.
Article Summary: Saleem Akbar S (46), a real estate businessman from Kodagu, was staying in a Koramangala hotel. He was driving the Audi, which had reportedly arrived near Sagar Fast Food at 2.36am while it was raining.

Article Title: Chennai shocker: Stalker beaten to death with iron rod by woman's friend at her home over relationship
Article Text:
A welder died after a fatal quarrel at a woman's house in Alapakkam.





CHENNAI: A 38-year-old welder, who had allegedly been stalking a woman and asking her to continue their relationship, died at Rajiv Gandhi Government General Hospital on Saturday after he was beaten with an iron rod following a quarrel at the woman’s house in Alapakkam. Police altered the case from attempt to murder to murder.Police identified the deceased as Jaishankar , a resident of Mudichur Road in West Tambaram. Police said he installed a gate at Poongodi’s house, 45, Kesavaraya Mudali Street, Alapakkam, about four months ago. The two subsequently became acquainted and remained in touch over the phone.Police said Poongodi blocked Jaishankar’s phone number about 10 days ago. Jaishankar went to her house and argued with her over the issue.Poongodi informed her acquaintance Damodaran, 33, about the quarrel. Damodaran arrived and asked Jaishankar to leave. When the argument continued, Damodaran picked up an iron rod from the house and struck Jaishankar on the head, critically injuring him.Hearing his cries, neighbors rushed him to the Government District Headquarters Hospital in Tambaram and later shifted him to the Rajiv Gandhi Government General Hospital for further treatment.Peerkankaranai police registered a case and arrested Damodaran and Poongodi. Both were remanded in judicial custody.Jaishankar died without responding to treatment on Saturday morning, after which police altered the case to murder. Further investigation is ongoing.
Article Summary: Police identified the deceased as Jaishankar, a resident of Mudichur Road in West Tambaram. Police said he installed a gate at Poongodi’s house, 45, Kesavaraya Mudali Street, Alapakkam, about four months ago.

Article Title: Uttarakhand MBBS scam: Fake certificates showed 'AI-generated pic' of freedom fighter
Article Text:
SIT officers during their probe in Dehradun. (PC: Dehradun Police)





DEHRADUN: A seven-member special investigation team (SIT) of Dehradun district police unit probing the alleged irregularities in MBBS admissions under the freedom-fighter dependents quota in Uttarakhand, has found that the certificates submitted by at least four students of unrelated families carried an AI-generated photograph of late freedom fighter Dharamveer, who was a resident of Dehradun's Jhanda Bazar area.Dehradun SP (rural) Jaya Baluni told TOI on Sunday, "While examining documents submitted by the four students, who availed admission under the freedom fighters' dependents quota in 2025, it was found that the photograph on the freedom fighter certificate was generated with the help of Artificial Intelligence... While the photo resembled the deceased, the other details including his father's name were incorrect. " Baluni is leading the SIT set up by Dehradun SSP Pramendra Dobal on Sept 18 after the irregularities surfaced.She further said that police found that all the four students had mentioned "Dharamveer as their paternal and maternal grandfather". "This, in spite of the fact that all four belonged to totally unrelated families who had no connection with him. Also, the mandatory personal details including address and mobile number mentioned in the admission forms by the four students were found to be non-existent.They had mentioned the same mobile number on their forms, which was unusual," added Baluni.All the four students are already facing FIRs registered in the city's Clement Town and Raipur police stations, but are yet to be summoned for questioning as the contact details were found to be fake.Following the findings, police had on Saturday called the late freedom fighter's son and grandson for questioning in the case. Police said they had no idea how his certificate was used; they said he died 12 years ago and, when alive, Dharamveer had instructed authorities not to transfer his pension to anyone after his death, and that even his direct family members had never claimed any benefit using his certificate. "We have asked the SDM office to provide us with related documents for examination," Baluni said, adding that "they now suspect an organised gang to be behind this crime."Another police officer, part of the SIT probe, said that the involvement of officials in the local administration as well as the management of medical colleges and universities was also suspected."It is questionable how those fake freedom fighter dependent certificates were issued on forged documents by govt offices. At the same time, questions arise on the verification done by the college/university management of the documents submitted by the students as all the four had mentioned the same person as their grandfather with fake mobile numbers and addresses. We'll soon question them too," said the officer, who did not wish to be named.
Article Summary: A special investigation team is probing alleged irregularities in MBBS admissions under the freedom-fighter dependents quota in Uttarakhand. The certificates submitted by at least four students of unrelated families carried an AI-generated photograph of late freedom fighter Dharamveer. Police said they had no idea how his certificate was used; they said he died 12 years ago.

Article Title: Resume triple talaq study: NCW to Keralam govt
Article Text:
National Commission for Women has requested the Kerala government to recommence its research on triple talaq





THIRUVANANTHAPURAM: National Commission for Women (NCW) has asked Keralam govt to withdraw the pause on the proposed study on the socio-legal impact of triple talaq among Muslim women in Malappuram. It sought chief secretary’s personal intervention to let the fieldwork proceed and file an action taken report within seven days.NCW member secretary Sudeep Jain’s letter to chief secretary Bishwanath Sinha on Sept 15 referred to the “reported decision” of the state govt to put the fieldwork on hold, despite state authorities having earlier agreed to facilitate it. NCW’s direct request to govt to withdraw the pause on the study marks a fresh turn in the issue.Jain pointed out that NCW had sought Malappuram district collector’s cooperation on July 1 and women and child development (WCD) department’s on July 20. “No legal, administrative or methodological objection was communicated, and the department had conveyed its willingness to assist,” the letter said.The study, commissioned under Section 10 of National Commission for Women Act, 1990, covers selected districts in Jammu & Kashmir, Assam, Uttar Pradesh, Maharashtra, Bihar and Keralam. It seeks to assess the lived experiences of women affected by triple talaq, the socio-legal impact of the law and the adequacy of support mechanisms.Keralam’s participation is important not only for understanding conditions within the state but also for ensuring that the study presents a balanced national picture and produces lessons relevant to policy and implementation across the country, NCW said.“This independent academic study safeguards confidentiality and informed participation. It neither seeks the state govt’s endorsement nor interferes with its administration,” the letter said.NCW said excluding one of the selected states would weaken the national evidence base and the study’s comparability.“If any specific concern exists, it may kindly be conveyed to the commission in writing with reasons,” said the letter.The development follows state WCD directorate’s earlier communication to Malappuram district administration that necessary assistance could be extended to the research team. Govt subsequently decided to keep the matter in abeyance.A senior official of minority welfare department said govt was examining the matter. “Since it involves field-level data collection among a particular section of the population in a specific district, govt would like to consider all relevant aspects before taking a final decision,” the official said.Govt’s decision to keep the study in abeyance assumes significance as Malappuram is the only district in Keralam specifically identified for primary data collection under the multi-state study. NCW’s letter says the project covers selected districts in six states, while the Keralam component involves data collection from affected Muslim women in Malappuram.
Article Summary: NCW has asked Keralam govt to withdraw the pause on the proposed study on the socio-legal impact of triple talaq among Muslim women in Malappuram. It sought chief secretary’s personal intervention to let the fieldwork proceed and file an action taken report within seven days.

Article Title: Annamalai steps up attack on Vijay over London trip, temple consecration
Article Text:
In photo: We The Leaders founder K Annamalai, Tamil Nadu CM Vijay





MADURAI: We The Leaders founder K Annamalai stepped up his attack on chief minister C Joseph Vijay on Sunday, targeting his London investment trip and TVK govt’s handling of the Meenakshi Amman temple consecration. He alleged there was poor planning, black-market sale of passes and preferential treatment for VIPs during the ceremony, held after 17 years.Speaking after a river clean-up drive at Madurai, Annamalai said that entry passes were sold “similar to cinema tickets in the black market,” while many ordinary devotees struggled to get the passes meant to be issued free of cost.“The activities of the HR&CE department are discouraging people from coming to temples. Kumbhabhishekam at Meenakshi Amman temple is an example of that kind of functioning,” he said.Annamalai said the HR&CE department would not continue if We The Leaders came to power. He also alleged that the assembly has transformed into a place where everyone, from a TVK MLA to speaker, exhibit their religious identities, instead of a forum for discussing public issues.On the CM’s overseas visit, Annamalai said Vijay need not travel to the UK seeking investments when its economy was growing at around 1%.“UK’s economy has shrunk smaller than India’s economy. In fact, Indian companies such as Tata and Mahindra are investing in the UK,’’ he said, adding that the CM should instead meet manufacturers in Madurai, Coimbatore and other industrial centres, offer incentives and help them expand within the state.
Article Summary: We The Leaders founder K Annamalai stepped up his attack on chief minister C Joseph Vijay on Sunday. He targeted his London investment trip and TVK govt’s handling of the Meenakshi Amman temple consecration. He alleged there was poor planning and black-market sale of passes.

Article Title: ‘Roachie’ joins dinner at Mumbai JW Marriott: Cardiologist finds baby cockroach, hotel responds
Article Text:
Cockroach on dinner table at Mumbai JW Marriott





MUMBAI: A Saturday night dinner at the Romano restaurant at JW Marriott took an unexpected turn after cardiologist Dr Ashok Seth spotted a baby cockroach on his table and said the sight forced him and his companions to leave without finishing their meal.Seth shared the incident on social media, tagging Maharashtra Food and Drug Administration (FDA) commissioner Tukaram Mundhe and the hotel.Seth said the cockroach, which he jokingly named “Roachie”, was on their table at Romano's, the Italian restaurant at JW Marriott Mumbai Sahar, on Saturday night.“Look who came for dinner unexpectedly. ‘Roachie’ - a baby cockroach was on our table wanting to share our dinner at the Romano restaurant at JW Marriott , Sahar , Mumbai, Saturday night!!!” he wrote in his post.Seth said the diners tried to persuade the insect to leave but it refused to move. Taking a humorous dig at the situation, he added, “Despite our persuasion ‘ Roachie’ refused to leave . Maybe wanted Piazza and not Pasta.”The incident, however, ended up taking away the diners' appetite. “But he really took our appetite away. We left,” Seth wrote.Seth also tagged Mundhe, FSSAI and JW Marriott in his post, adding, “Thankfully we are in Mr Munde’s , territory and he most likely will look into this also.”Marriott Bonvoy Assist responded to Seth's post, saying it took the matter seriously and wanted to look into the incident. “Hello Dr. Ahok, thank you for letting us know. We take this matter seriously. We would like to look into it for you. Could you please DM us your first, last name, and your confirmation number?” the account replied.The incident comes as Maharashtra's FDA, under Mundhe, has been carrying out an intensified food-safety enforcement drive across the state.FDA teams had conducted many raids and taken action against food establishments over alleged hygiene and food-safety violations, including pest infestations.Mundhe's name has also figured in several recent social-media complaints involving alleged food-hygiene lapses.In August, actor Shweta Tiwari tagged the FDA chief after claiming she found a cockroach following a cold-drink delivery.The latest incident also comes shortly after FSSAI issued notices to two five-star hotels in Delhi's Aerocity, including JW Marriott, over reported food-safety and hygiene deficiencies.At JW Marriott in Aerocity, inspectors recorded 59 deficiencies, including pest activity, improper food storage and other issues.
Article Summary: Cardiologist Dr Ashok Seth spotted a baby cockroach on his table and said the sight forced him and his companions to leave without finishing their meal. He shared the incident on social media, tagging Maharashtra Food and Drug Administration (FDA) commissioner Tukaram Mundhe and the hotel.

Article Title: 'Ab nikaal ke bata gadi': A month before Gurgaon hit-and-run case, men chased, harassed Bhopal biker
Article Text:
In Bhopal, biker Abida Rana encountered a troubling situation when two men in a car relentlessly pursued her on Nabibagh Road





BHOPAL: Nearly a month before a woman biker’s hit-and-run incident in Gurgaon sparked widespread outrage, 23-year-old Bhopal-based biker, Abida Rana, had faced a similar ordeal in the city, with two men in a car chasing her for around 600-700 metres, abusing and repeatedly blocking her way.The ordeal took place on Aug 2 on Nabibagh Road, under Nishatpura police station limits. Abida had shared a video of the Bhopal ordeal on her Instagram handle on Aug 5, which is being widely circulated now.According to Abida, she was around 5 km from home when on the Nishatpura-Nabibagh stretch, two men crossing the road allegedly stopped their car in the middle of the road near the divider and began abusing her without any apparent reason.One of the men allegedly shouted, “Ab nikaal ke bata gadi.” With vehicles behind her honking, Abida said she was forced to move around the car from the left side.The men allegedly changed course and started following her, and repeatedly blocking her way.Abida said she became panicked and angry and told the men that the police station was only 1-2 km away and warned them that she would complain if they continued following and threatening her.When she tried to drive away, the men allegedly blocked her path from the right side as well. She then drove towards the police station, claiming the men continued chasing her and hurling abuses. They left just before the police station.Later, the men were called up to the police station and cops warned the men not to approach her again and made them write an apology before allowing them to leave. No FIR was registered as Abida had opted not to pursue a criminal case, cops said.
Article Summary: Bhopal-based biker Abida Rana, 23, faced a similar ordeal in the city. Two men in a car chased her for around 600-700 metres, abusing and repeatedly blocking her way. Abida had shared a video of the Bhopal ordeal on her Instagram handle.

Article Title: Kolkata shocker: Bedridden man bludgeoned to death by brother over property dispute
Article Text:
The house where the incident took place





KOLKATA: A 28-year-old bedridden man was found bludgeoned to death at his home around noon on Sunday. The house too was found ransacked with gold ornaments and other costly items, worth Rs 1.5 lakh, missing from the almirahs.Cops said the victim’s elder brother has been arrested for murdering the 28-year-old following a property dispute and desperation over the victim — bedridden since 2017 after an accident — ‘hurtling the family into a financial crisis following repeated surgeries’. “He then threw away items around the room to make it look like a robbery,” an officer said.The victim has been identified as Balaram Rajbanshi, who underwent a brain surgery a few days ago. The incident was reported from near the Charigram Sri Ramkrishna Ashram Adarsha Balika Vidyalaya in Raghunathpur area of Teghoria under Baguiati PS.Police said that around 12.50 pm, Balaram was found lying in a pool of blood on his bed with severe injuries on his forehead. Cops said he was found unconscious on his bed by his mother who had just returned from work. “He had reportedly been bedridden following a surgery.Police immediately reached the spot. The room was found open, the almirahs unlocked, and clothes and other articles scattered on the floor. A lacerated injury was noticed on the deceased’s scalp,” said cops.“During probe, we found that his elder brother, Krishna Rajbanshi (33), had murdered him over a property dispute and attempted to portray the incident as theft. The accused has confessed to have committed the crime. He will be produced in a court on Monday with a prayer for police custody,” said a senior officer of Bidhannagar Police. The body has been sent to R G Kar Medical College and Hospital for post-mortem.According to police and family, the incident occurred between 8 am and noon. Balaram, who could barely recognise family members and communicate with them, was alone at home alongside their pet dog, a mongrel, after his family members left for their daily work in the morning. The victim’s mother works as a domestic help, while his father runs a fish trade. His brother, the accused Krishna, worked as a food delivery agent.The family was trying to complete the construction of their two-storey house. While the first floor was nearing completion, money constraints stopped the work on the first floor. Krishna got married a little over a year ago and his wife was staying with her own family as she had conceived recently.To prevent the pet dog from raising an alarm, the accused had locked the animal inside an adjacent room.Family members, led by the accused Krishna, initially alleged that approximately Rs 1.5 lakh in cash, alongside gold ornaments and other high-value personal belongings, was looted. “The accused hit his brother repeatedly and bludgeoned him on the head at the exact spots where he had stitches from the operation to ensure a quick death,” said an officer.
Article Summary: A 28-year-old bedridden man was found bludgeoned to death at his home around noon on Sunday. The house too was found ransacked with gold ornaments and other costly items, worth Rs 1.5 lakh, missing from the almirahs. Cops said the victim’s elder brother has been arrested for murdering him following a property dispute and desperation over the victim.

Article Title: IIT-Bombay suicide case: Institute director Shireesh Kedare meets protesting students, ‘signs’ list of 18 demands
Article Text:
Students gathered in large numbers at IIT-Bombay main gate to protest against the death by suicide of BTech student Sahil

Poll Vote & Share your view What should be the main priority for IIT Bombay after the student protest? Student safety and support Independent investigation Better communication with students Stronger student welfare measures 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion





MUMBAI: In a late-night three-hour meeting on Sunday, IIT-Bombay director Shireesh Kedare spoke to the students who gathered in large numbers at the institute’s main gate to protest against the death by suicide of BTech student Sahil Wakode (20).In the meeting, which was recorded live by the students, the institute’s administration discussed 18 demands put forth by the protesters and signed it. An institute official said that the discussions will continue and “due process will be followed”.The institute’s Board of Governors is scheduled to meet on Monday to discuss the issue. An open house with students is also expected to be held on the same day.Protests erupted on the Powai campus on Friday night after Wakode, a second-year student of energy science and engineering, ended his life hours after he was caught using a mobile phone during the institute’s mid-semester examination. He allegedly uploaded the exam paper on an AI platform for answers. This was the third case of suicide on the campus this year.While the institute, in a statement, mentioned that no action was initiated against Wakode, many claimed that he was threatened with suspension.Among students’ demands, suspension of Prof Suryanarayana Doolla, Sahil’s teacher and also the invigilator of the exam, was the foremost.Sahil’s family had filed an FIR against Doolla and ‘other institute officials’, accusing them of abetment and harassment over the last three months.The students also asked for an open apology for ‘defaming’ Sahil and an open house with all the stakeholders before Sept 22. The list of demands also includes an independent investigation committee with student representatives and external members recommended by them, suspension of officials who are found guilty after the probe, and a fair compensation for the families. Students have also sought a code of conduct and sensitisation for professors.Amid the ongoing protest, IIT-B’s faculty forum has come out in support of Doolla. In a statement issued on Sunday, the forum, while mourning the loss of life of the student and extending condolences to the family, strongly expressed their solidarity with the professor.The forum said, “...the professor was discharging his duties in line with the institute’s Senate approved academic policies currently in force”. It added, “Prof Doolla was invigilating in the examination on Friday, when he observed that a student was indulging in an academic malpractice... As part of the institute approved procedure, he reported the incident to institute authorities for further action in the matter. ”The faculty forum added that they are distressed with the tarnishing of the reputation of their colleague who was merely discharging his duties.Meanwhile, the institute is planning to replace the ceiling fans with wall-mounted ones in its student hostels. Sources said the plan had been under consideration for the past two months and was finalised recently. The first batch of wall-mounted fans seemed to have arrived on campus, students claimed.Replacing the fans was among the measures the institute had assured students it would undertake in July, following the death by suicide of another student from the same hostel.
Article Summary: In a late-night three-hour meeting on Sunday, IIT-Bombay director Shireesh Kedare spoke to the students. In the meeting, which was recorded live by the students, the institute’s administration discussed 18 demands put forth by the protesters and signed it. This was the third case of suicide on the campus this year.

Article Title: Late-night call, brutal attack: Property dealer killed in Delhi's Kalkaji, brother beaten when he rushed to spot
Article Text:
48-year-old property dealer beaten to death in Kalkaji





NEW DELHI: A 48-year-old property dealer was beaten to death, allegedly by a group of people, in southeast Delhi's Kalkaji late Saturday night.Police suspect a property dispute and disagreement over construction work at a building may have led to the incident.A mother and her daughter as well as a man were apprehended over the incident. Cops received a PCR call regarding a quarrel at L-8, Kalkaji, at 12.03am Sunday.A team reached the area and found a scuffle had taken place between the residents of a building. Manjeet Singh alias Bunty and his brother, Dilbag Singh, were injured and taken to AIIMS Trauma Centre, where the former was declared dead.His family said he received a phone call at 11pm, after which he left his house on his scooty. Around 20 minutes later, Dilbag was informed by locals that a group of people was beating up his brother.When Dilbag reached the spot, he allegedly found Manjeet lying unconscious on a pavement with his shirt torn and bruises to his chest and neck."They dragged me to the ground and started kicking me. My sister threw herself on me and begged them to stop. They held her by the hair and shoved her aside," Dilbag alleged.He suffered a fractured right leg and injuries to his forehead and shoulder.Manjeet is survived by his two teenage sons, Lishant (15) and Fateh (14).One of Lishant's friends, 17-year-old Daljeet, was among the first to alert the family. "I was returning home when I saw Manjeet uncle in a heated argument with a few men, which turned into a fight. I ran home after being punched while trying to intervene," he said.Police said a civil dispute relating to the building is pending in court. They are also probing whether ongoing construction on the premises was connected to the attack."Before the scuffle, a PCR call had been made regarding alleged illegal construction at the building. We had informed MCD about it earlier as well," a police officer said.There was no response from MCD till late Sunday.Dilbag claimed he saw members of a family standing with suspected attackers and egging them on to beat up his brother. Police are checking CCTV footage, said DCP, southeast.
Article Summary: A 48-year-old property dealer was beaten to death, allegedly by a group of people. Manjeet Singh alias Bunty and his brother, Dilbag Singh, were injured and taken to AIIMS Trauma Centre. Police suspect a property dispute and disagreement over construction work at a building may have led to the incident.

Article Title: 4 men putting up CCTV cameras die after dumper hits crane, auto in southeast Delhi; 2 injured
Article Text:
The deceased Umesh (23),auto driver, Praveen (35), technician, Anup (26), worker

Dumper driver escapes, still at large

Poll Vote & Share your view Do you think the company responsible for the installation should be held accountable for the incident? Yes, they should take responsibility No, it's the driver's fault 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion





NEW DELHI: Four people installing CCTV cameras for Delhi Traffic Police were killed and two were injured when a dumper truck collided with a stationary crane and a parked autorickshaw in Sarita Vihar early Sunday morning.The deceased were identified as Umesh (23), Praveen (35), Suraj (34) and Anup (26). They were residents of Sangam Vihar and Munirka. Two others, Akash (20) and Khem Singh (40), suffered injuries and are under treatment. A seventh person on the spot, identified as Sudhir, was unhurt. The six were taken to a nearby hospital but four of them succumbed to injuries.Police said that on Road No. 13 in Sarita Vihar at 3.20am, the dumper coming from Noida rammed into the crane and a parked autorickshaw while the workers were busy with the installation.Of the four deceased, Suraj worked as an HR manager in the private firm. Praveen was a technician in the same firm and Anup too was an employee. Umesh was an autorickshaw driver.Akash and Khem Singh were also working for the same company. Praveen, Anup and Akash were cousins.A response was also sought from the firm which had assigned the six to carry out the CCTV installation, but it is yet to come.The dumper driver fled and has not yet been traced. Searches are on to arrest him.The vehicle bore a Haryana registration number.A relative of Umesh alleged that there were inadequate safety measures in place for the workers installing the CCTV cameras.An inquiry has revealed that seven people were on the spot. Two workers were standing on the crane and installing the cameras, while two others were standing nearby. One person was inside an autorickshaw and another was standing beside it. The seventh person, Sudhir, was standing some distance away.According to the families of the deceased workers, the people present at the spot had seen the approaching dumper and waved to indicate that the driver must stop, but he did not heed their signal.Police also found out that 50 metres ahead of the spot, there was a fluorescent barricade placed to indicate that work was going on, but the dumper driver did not heed that either.When the dumper hit the crane, the two workers who were fixing the cameras fell down. The impact was so severe that the crane’s tyres burst. The autorickshaw too was damaged.Praveen’s brother, Brijesh, said that while the two workers were fixing the cameras, Praveen was using a laptop to monitor and adjust the cameras. The road where the accident took place was busy and heavy vehicles frequently passed through the stretch at a high speed during the night.The families of the victims learnt about the tragedy from various sources. Some of them got phone calls. Others were informed by people who visited their homes.
Article Summary: Four people installing CCTV cameras for Delhi Traffic Police were killed and two were injured when a dumper truck collided with a stationary crane and a parked autorickshaw. The deceased were identified as Umesh (23), Praveen (35), Suraj (34) and Anup (26) Two others, Akash (20) and Khem Singh (40), suffered injuries and are under treatment. A seventh person on the spot, identified as Sudhir, was unhurt.

Article Title: Akal Takht expels SGPC member Amarjit Chawla for allegations concerning ‘cardinal sin of adultery’
Article Text:
Akal Takht jathedar announces excommunication of SGPC member Amarjit Singh Chawla and Golden Temple additional head granthi Malkit Singh





CHANDIGARH: The Akal Takht on Sunday excommunicated Shiromani Gurdwara Parbandhak Committee (SGPC) member Amarjit Singh Chawla and Golden Temple additional head granthi Malkit Singh from Khalsa Panth over allegations of rape and harassment. Both have been barred for life from working in Sikh institutions.Akal Takht officiating Jathedar Kuldip Singh Gargajj, who is also the Jathedar of Takht Kesgarh Sahib, announced the decisions from the ‘faseel’ (podium) of Akal Takht following a meeting at its secretariat in Amritsar. The meeting included Takht Damdama Sahib Jathedar Tek Singh, Golden Temple granthi Kewal Singh, Akal Takht granthi Gurbakhshish Singh and one of the Panj Pyaras, Mangal Singh.Giani Gargajj said the allegations damaged the dignity of Sikh institutions. He cited the Panth-approved Sikh Rehat Maryada, which mandates excommunication for any of the four “Bajjar Kurehits“ (cardinal sins): dishonouring or cutting hair, consuming halal meat, adultery and tobacco use. “Chawla remains excommunicated until he proves his innocence and appears before the Akal Takht,” Giani Gargajj said.The action follows an Aug 21 FIR registered at Anandpur Sahib police station.A woman alleged Chawla raped her repeatedly between March and May at Anandpur Sahib and Amritsar after the SGPC provided her accommodation upon her Nov 2025 return to India. She also alleged Chawla threatened to kill her if she spoke out.Chawla denied the charges as a “completely false, baseless” conspiracy, but resigned from the SGPC and his post as Shiromani Akali Dal senior vice-president.The complainant also accused Malkit Singh and Takht Kesgarh Sahib driver Mohan Singh of sending her obscene messages. The SGPC suspended both on Sept 17. Though the FIR named only Chawla, the woman alleged misconduct by others.According to the FIR, the woman said she even approached Akal Takht Jathedar about the matter “several times” and “showed the proofs, but no action was taken”. Responding to a question on this, Giani Gargajj said, “I meet thousands of sangat (devotees) every day. That bibi (woman) met me in the same manner. She met me casually. She talked to me about Malkit Singh, mentioning that he did some inappropriate chat. She did not talk to me about Amarjit Singh or anyone other. She spoke to me verbally. Despite this, understanding my responsibility, I asked the Shiromani Gurdwara Parbandhak Committee to remove this man from the Akal Takht. And as far as I know, after that, he did not perform any service at the Akal Takht Sahib. If the woman had told me about Amarjit Singh, I would have taken strict action in the matter.”Announcing the excommunication of Malkit Singh, Akal Takht noted that when a person is serving in a responsible Sikh position, he carries a great responsibility towards the community and the religion to always maintain his character and moral conduct in accordance with the Guru’s teachings.” “The levelling of allegations against a person occupying such a responsible position brings collective dishonour to the community. Therefore, Malkit Singh is excommunicated from the Khalsa Panth. All Sikh sangats are directed not to maintain any kind of association with him. A complete ban is imposed on Malkit Singh from working in Sikh institutions for the remainder of his life,” Akal Takht addedGiani Gargaj called for an impartial police investigation into the case and urged the SGPC to conduct its own high-level inquiry.
Article Summary: Jathedar Kuldip Singh Gargajj announced the decisions from the ‘faseel’ (podium) of Akal Takht. The action follows an Aug 21 FIR registered at Anandpur Sahib police station. A woman alleged Chawla raped her repeatedly between March and May. She also accused Malkit Singh and Takht Kesgarh Sahib driver Mohan Singh.

Article Title: Handcuffed, phones seized: Mumbai student claim cops searched home over pro-Palestine campaign
Article Text:
A student claims police searched her home for nine hours without a warrant





MUMBAI: Postgraduate student Harshada Borade has alleged that Bandra police's anti-terrorism cell searched her home for over nine hours without a warrant and mistreated her friends after she took part in a pro-Palestine kite-flying campaign on Sept 15.Borade said the house owner has since asked her to vacate.Borade, in a video posted on Sunday, alleged that at least 15 cops searched her residence from 5pm on Friday until 3am on Saturday without serving a legal notice or producing a warrant.She claimed plainclothes personnel refused to show identification, forcibly entered her personal space, examined her notebooks and diaries, recorded book titles and photographed and videographed her belongings.Bandra police have not registered an FIR against Borade and are gathering details and conducting a background check on her. DCP (West Zone-2) Mohit Garg said an inquiry was under way "in accordance with procedures established by law".Indian People In Solidarity With Palestine (IPSP), of which Borade is an activist, said six to seven plainclothes personnel identifying themselves as cops arrived at her residence.It alleged that Borade was detained without written notice and later taken back to the residence.IPSP alleged that the search ended after 2.30am on Sept 19 and that Borade's friends were manhandled and abused. It claimed two volunteers were handcuffed, their phones confiscated, and those present threatened with legal action and physical violence.According to IPSP, the panchnama linked the search to a nationwide kite campaign expressing solidarity with children in Gaza. It said the document listed books and quotations by Bhagat Singh and Savitribai Phule among the items found.IPSP also alleged that the panchnama stated the search was not pre-planned but was authorised by senior police officials after personnel found Borade's "behaviour suspicious".
Article Summary: Postgraduate student Harshada Borade claims police searched her home for nine hours without a warrant. Borade took part in a pro-Palestine kite-flying campaign on Sept 15. Police have not registered an FIR against Borade and are gathering details.

Article Title: Hyderabad horror: Auto driver beaten to death in Rs 10 change dispute
Article Text:
An auto-rickshaw driver was allegedly beaten to death in Vattapally on Sunday evening (AI image)





HYDERABAD: An auto-rickshaw driver was allegedly beaten to death following an argument over Rs 10 change in Vattapally, under the jurisdiction of Rajendranagar police station, on Sunday evening, according to ANI.Police said an altercation broke out between the driver and a group of people over the change amount, following which he was allegedly assaulted.Police, along with local AIMIM leaders, reached the spot after being alerted about the incident.A police official said, “We have registered a case, and investigation is underway.”
Article Summary: An auto-rickshaw driver was allegedly beaten to death following an argument over Rs 10 change in Vattapally, under the jurisdiction of Rajendranagar police station, on Sunday evening. Police said an altercation broke out between the driver and a group of people over the change amount.

Article Title: 25 years after man’s murder, son kills one of the accused
Article Text:
The police apprehended Balamurugan and eleven others within hours, but Saravanan succumbed to his injuries shortly after arriving at the hospital (Representative image)





MADURAI: A 26-year-old man avenged his father’s murder after 25 years by hacking to death Sappani Saravanan, 57, one of the accused in the 2001 killing of Pushparaj, near Solai Alagupuram in Madurai on Saturday.Police arrested Pushparaj’s son Balamurugan and 11 others within five hours of the killing.Police said Pushparaj, a notorious rowdy from West Masi Street, was murdered by an eight-member gang in 2001.Saravanan, a resident of Sappani Kovil Street in Solai Alagupuram, was one of the accused in the case, while five others have since died.Three of them were murdered by Pushparaj’s friends, police said.A preliminary investigation found that Balamurugan had been waiting for an opportunity to kill Saravanan.Around 8.15am on Saturday, Balamurugan and his accomplices arrived in an autorickshaw and two-wheelers in front of a seat cover shop near Jaihindpuram Second Main Road.Armed with knives, they surrounded Saravanan and his family members and attacked him, inflicting injuries on his head, abdomen, hip and hands.When Saravanan’s wife and son tried to intervene, the gang threatened and assaulted them. Saravanan was rushed to Government Rajaji Hospital, where doctors declared him dead.A special team of Jaihindpuram police led by inspector Boominathan under the supervision of DCP (South) A G Inigo Thivyan arrested 12 accused within five hours. They were subsequently remanded in judicial custody on Sunday.Police are investigating further.
Article Summary: Sappani Saravanan, 57, one of the accused in the 2001 killing of Pushparaj, near Solai Alagupuram in Madurai on Saturday. Police arrested his son Balamurugan and 11 others within five hours of the killing.

Article Title: Umar Khalid film gets private Kurla screening after Versova cancellation
Article Text:
A documentary on jailed activist Umar Khalid was screened privately in Kurla after a planned public viewing was cancelled





MUMBAI: A day after a planned screening of a 2024 documentary on jailed activist Umar Khalid was cancelled in Versova following alleged intervention by Mumbai Police , the film was screened at a private event in Kurla on Sunday.More than 20 people attended the invite-only screening at a community centre, where the documentary Prisoner No. 626710 is Present, directed by Lalit Vachnani, was followed by a reading of poetry by Gulfisha Fatima, a co-accused with Khalid in the 2020 Delhi riots case.The Versova screening had been organised by Mumbai-based activist-influencers Prashant Purandir and Shrishti Khanna. They alleged that people in civilian clothes claiming to be police first approached the venue manager and pressured him to cancel the event. They said the manager subsequently received a call from the superintendent of police and that a police vehicle later arrived at the venue.“We were not given any reason or told that police permission was required,” Purandir and Khanna said, alleging that the intervention amounted to intimidation. They also claimed that a Bandra venue they had earlier considered was “threatened” and that several other venues declined to host the screening after learning that the film was about Khalid.The documentary has also faced cancellations elsewhere. A planned screening at NLSIU, Bengaluru, on Sept 14 was postponed and later scrapped following objections from ABVP, while a screening at IIIT-Hyderabad scheduled for Sept 18 was cancelled after Central Board of Film Certification (CBFC) said on X that the event would be “in violation of the Cinematograph Act”.Bombay HC lawyer Chandni Chawla said CBFC certification requirements apply to public or commercial screenings and that private screenings are not governed by the Cinematograph Act.The Kurla organiser, Abhishek, said he was advised not to publicise the event as a precaution and kept it invite-only and free of charge. “That way no one could argue that the screening was public and so the film requires certification. The film is not banned. It’s ridiculous that we should be made to feel afraid to watch it,” he said.The documentary covers the events preceding Khalid’s arrest and his incarceration. Khalid, who has been in custody since Sept 2020 in the Delhi riots conspiracy case, is facing trial.
Article Summary: More than 20 people attended the invite-only screening at a community centre. Prisoner No. 626710 is Present, directed by Lalit Vachnani, was followed by a reading of poetry by Gulfisha Fatima, a co-accused with Khalid.

Article Title: Kalyan builder gets death threat from aide of absconding ex-cop in gang-rape involving ex-BJP MLA
Article Text:
In photo: Ex- cop Shailesh Patil





KALYAN: The trouble of former police constable Shailesh Patil, who is on the run in a gang-rape case registered against him and former BJP MLA Narendra Pawar, may increase further as an alleged aide of Patil has threatened a Kalyan-based builder, Rohit Dixit, asking him to withdraw another case filed against Patil in court or face dire consequences, the builder has alleged.Dixit approached Khadakpada police, alleging that Yogesh Harad made a WhatsApp call to him on Friday, abused him and pressured him to withdraw his complaint against Patil and Prashant Deshmukh. Dixit alleged that Harad threatened him with serious consequences when he refused to withdraw the complaint.Based on the complaint, Khadakpada police registered a non-cognisable report under Sections 352 and 351(2) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS). Police are probing the allegations and are also expected to ascertain whether Harad allegedly acted at the instance of Patil or Deshmukh.Patil and Deshmukh have faced criminal cases in the past, according to police records. Patil is currently wanted in connection with the gang-rape case registered by Padgha police following a complaint by a 22-year-old married woman. Pawar has also been named as a co-accused. Both are yet to be arrested.Patil had previously faced at least four criminal cases, including allegations relating to sexual assault, fraud involving a South African national and extortion.Meanwhile, UBT MLA and Kalyan Sampark Pramukh of UBT Varun Sardesai visited Kalyan and questioned the police over the delay in arresting Pawar and Patil. He demanded Pawar's arrest and questioned why both accused remained at large despite the registration of the FIR.Sardesai said that political opponents often face immediate action when allegations are made against them, and questioned why action had not yet been taken in this case despite the complainant coming forward with serious allegations of gang rape.
Article Summary: Shailesh Patil is on the run in a gang-rape case registered against him and former BJP MLA Narendra Pawar. An alleged aide of Patil has threatened a Kalyan- based builder, Rohit Dixit, asking him to withdraw another case filed against Patil in court or face dire consequences.
